M101 GN7 requires min 12"x12" access to dampers, M301 KN4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC maintenance, and M501 requires approved access with a permanent label reading FIRE DAMPER in letters min 1/2" high — while NONE of the ten A550-A556 guestroom RCPs draws one, including A555 view 02 which governs this room. 115-room omission, RFI candidate and a CO-inspection exposure. M401 KN5 INTERIOR PTAC WALL GRILLE — no DB row (the DB carries only the exterior louver). M401 prints KN1 'grille painted to match EXTERIOR wall' and KN5 'grille painted to match INTERIOR wall' and never says whether that is one grille painted two colours or two grilles. It decides whether a separate painted grille exists inside the finished room and whose paint scope the room-side face is. Emitted sheets-only, FLAGGED.

CONNECTED ROOM EDGE CONTROLLER — no DB row. Named twice in A555 kn47 and once in E101 GN #8, and nowhere else: no mark, no legend symbol, no E-series schedule, no count, no location. Emitted sheets-only, FLAGGED. Also missing set-wide and worth Austin knowing: no telecom riser diagram, rack elevation, port count or head-end equipment schedule exists anywhere, so several LV lines can only be punched against an integrator submittal.

UNDERCABINET-LIGHTING OUTLET (kn50) IS ON ROOM 101 AT HIGH AND NO SHEET PLACES IT — expected quantity is ZERO. A555 governs the whole QQ family and its placed-keynote list for views 04/04.1 is verbatim '3, 10, 14, 15, 16, 24, 25, 28, 36, 44, 45, 46, 47, 51'; kn50 is absent. A550 defines kn50 in the legend only and never places it. packages/electrical.md §5.1.1 repair CR-2 restricts kn50 to the 7 accessible keys — floor 1 that is room 118 ONLY — and records that the DB is stale (it still carries it on 104 as well). DOORBELL (kn28) IS ON ROOM 101 AND THIS IS NOT A COMMUNICATION-FEATURES KEY — expected quantity is ZERO. A100's Guestroom Matrix floor-1 column reads 'Queen Queen (Wide), CD = 1 S' with no HI suffix, and the 'Queen Queen, HI' row is EMPTY on floor 1; the single floor-1 hearing-impaired key is 'King Studio, HI = 1 T', one of 104/106/108/110/112/114. PTAC MARK — M401 line 24 verbatim: 'PTAC-1 on most rooms; PTAC-2 on the higher-load types — detail 01/02 show PTAC-2', and detail 01 is 'QQ, QQ, Ext., QQ Conn.' which includes room 101. NEW EVIDENCE FOR THE RFI: E103 row 14 'Queen Queen (Wide)' (201/301) is byte-identical in every load column — 535 / 1605 / 850 / - / - / 9256 — yet is assigned Panel A. The two rows differ only in the connecting door and the panel letter. Neither position adopted. Closable in thirty seconds by reading the panel card in 101.

WALL RECEPTACLES/DATA PORTS TO [B]E MOUNTED @ 12" TYPICAL U.N.O', byte-identical on A531, A532, A532.1 and A533 — five bath sheets) vs 18" AFF (E101 spec #18, E101 symbol legend, G400 detail 02 'ALL RECEPTACLES SHALL BE 18" A.F.F. M201 = polypropylene louver kit (colour by architect); M501 det.9 = aluminium architectural grille factory-painted; M401 KN1 = furnished with unit, painted to match exterior; A200 kn8 and AS103 = aluminium louver INTEGRAL TO THE WINDOW SYSTEM (glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory). critic.summary: The spine is sound and unusually well-sourced — the PTAC mark conflict, the panel-letter conflict (E103 row 15 transcribes exactly), the EF-1 fan-vs-grille conflict, the M305 riser arithmetic (2,450 CFM / 49 inlets, 850 CFM fan shortfall), the WAG-30 view-07 location conflict, the kn50 and doorbell zero-quantity corrections, and the shower/lav mark carries all check out against the sheets. No rough-in leaked in: every emitted line is testable at a visible point and the two arguable ones (FD/VD, gate valves) state the argument. Every verifyAtPunch is a real action — none is "verify installed". Room typing is right: A100's matrix reads "Queen Queen (Wide), CD = 1 S", OV-001 is narrowed to label-only so room_type stays QQ Wide Connecting, and the accessible/HI exclusions are correctly applied. But two defects are serious enough to stop the walk: the lavatory deck-hole test is inverted against what P104 actually prints and would generate false write-ups at 115 keys, and A555 KN30 is cited as placed on view 08 when A555 places no such keynote anywhere — the identical failure mode the list correctly caught for kn50. Four punch-visible devices are missing entirely (entry/room light switch, dishwasher switch under the sink, quad receptacles, side-wall sprinkler heads), and three lines resolve a live two-reading conflict silently, which is the one thing Austin's rules forbid.
missingDevices: Entry / room light switch(es) — E400 lists 'switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)'; the A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND prints 'SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY'; A555 kn3 restricts the nightlight switch to 'IN BATHROOM LOCATIONS ONLY', which presupposes non-bath switches exist. No line, no count, no height. The walker flips every switch in the room and has nothing to record against.

Dishwasher switch in the cabinet under the sink — E101 General Note 4 verbatim: 'Dishwasher switches in cabinet under sink.' Operable, punch-visible (open the cabinet door), and it ties directly to the unresolved SK-3/SK-4 sink question, since A555 tags 902 DISHWASHER on the working wall.

Quad receptacle — the A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND prints 'OUTLET - QUAD' and 'OUTLET - QUAD - GFI' as guestroom symbols, and E101's symbol legend carries 'quad/quad-duplex receptacle'. The list carries only 'Convenience duplex receptacles' with no note that a quad may be installed.

Side-wall sprinkler head — the same legend prints THREE sprinkler symbols: 'SIDE WALL SPRINKLER HEAD', 'SPRINKLER HEAD' and 'SIDE WALL SPRINKLER HEAD (D)'. The sprinkler line's 'where' is ceilings only.
Water-closet supply stop — the lavatory line's verify covers 'both stops'; nothing covers the WC angle stop, which is the visible trim a walker wipes for weep.

defects.line: Plumbing — 'Lavatory faucet — Delta 581LF-GPM-PP, manual, 1.0 GPM, less 3-hole escutcheon' (and the dependent 'REJECT CHECK — unapproved lav substitution' line)
defects.problem: The line turns a deck-hole count into the pass/fail discriminator — 'COUNT THE DECK HOLES — 3 = as designed, 1 = the unapproved substitution' — on the assertion that 'P104's Delta 581LF is a 3-HOLE trim'. P104 states no such thing. What P104 prints is 'Faucet Delta 581LF-GPM-PP manual 1.0 GPM, less 3-hole escutcheon'. 'Less' means supplied WITHOUT the 3-hole escutcheon, i.e. the deck plate that would let a single-hole faucet cover a 3-hole deck is deleted — which reads toward a SINGLE-hole install, the opposite of what the line claims. No sheet in the set states a deck hole count for the guestroom vanity. The REJECT CHECK line inherits it verbatim ('changes the countertop cutout from 3-hole to 1-hole on 115 vanity tops') and escalates it to 'If you see ... a single-handle single-hole Moen — STOP ... log it as unapproved.' A walker following this writes up correctly-installed faucets in every room he enters. This is an inference the package already made (packages/fire-appliance.md §4.2 'P104's Delta is 3-hole') and the reconciler imported it without checking it against the sheet — exactly the failure the SHEETS-GOVERN rule exists to catch.
defects.correction: Strike the hole-count pass/fail from both lines. Faucet line note: 'P104 prints only "less 3-hole escutcheon" — no deck hole count is stated on any sheet, and "less" reads toward a single-hole deck. RECORD the make, model and hole count as data; do not judge either.' Verify step: 'Read the faucet make and model off the trim and write down the deck hole count; run 60 s, no drip at spout or under deck.' REJECT CHECK line: the discriminator is the MAKE — American Standard Studio bowl or Moen M-Dura 9417F12/9419F12 instead of Decolav Callensia 1402-CWH + Delta 581LF-GPM-PP — not the hole count.
defects.citation: P104 rows L-3 and L-4, REMARKS column: 'Faucet Delta 581LF-GPM-PP manual 1.0 GPM, less 3-hole escutcheon'; packages/fire-appliance.md:402-403 and :407 (the source of the imported 3-hole reading)

defects.line: Mechanical — 'Packaged terminal A/C unit, G.E., 208/1/60...' (src 'A555 KN1/KN30 view 08') and 'PTAC mounting condition — min 3-1/4" AFF, unit edge above carpet tiles' (src 'A555 KN30 ("EDGE OF PTAC ABOVE CARPET TILES")')
defects.problem: A555 does not place keynote 30 anywhere. A555's placed-keynote lists are: view 01 = 1, 4, 5, 11, 12, 21, 32, 33 · view 02 = 18, 19, 7, 4, 1 · view 03 = 22 · views 04/04.1 = 3, 10, 14, 15, 16, 24, 25, 28, 36, 44, 45, 46, 47, 51 · view 05 = 1, 11, 14, 36, 47 · view 06 = 12, 16 · view 07 = 4, 20, 23, 24, 28, 39, 41, 51 · view 08 = 1, 4 · view 09 = 1, 9, 11, 14, 36, 47. Keynote 30 is defined in the A550 legend ('EDGE OF PTAC ABOVE CARPET TILES') and never placed on A555. The PTAC line cites 'A555 KN1/KN30 view 08' — view 08 carries keynotes 1 and 4 only. This is the identical failure the list correctly caught and corrected for kn50, applied to kn30 and missed. Worse, the whole 'PTAC mounting condition' line's carpet-tile requirement rests on it, and its verify step ('confirm carpet stops under the unit edge, not over it') is therefore not backed by anything placed on the sheet that governs this room.
defects.correction: Strike KN30 from both src strings. PTAC line src becomes 'M201 schedule; M401 det.01; M301; M501 det.9; A555 KN1 view 08'. The mounting line keeps M501 det.9 ('min 3-1/4" AFF', field-built sub-base, condensate down wall) and must be re-flagged: 'THE CARPET-TILE RELATIONSHIP IS NOT PLACED ON THE SHEET THAT GOVERNS THIS ROOM. A550 keynote 30 reads "EDGE OF PTAC ABOVE CARPET TILES" but A555 never places it — its finish plan (view 03) carries only keynote 22. Record the as-built relationship; do not write it up. SETTLES IT: re-read A555 view 03 / view 08 on the source PDF for a keynote-30 leader, the same re-read that closed kn50.'
defects.citation: A555.md lines 74, 95, 104, 110-114, 120-124 (per-view placed-keynote lists); A550.md line 148 (kn30 defined in the legend only)

defects.line: MISSING — no line for the entry / room light switch(es)
defects.problem: The list carries a bathroom light switch and a garbage-disposal switch and nothing else. E400 explicitly lists per-room 'switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)'. The A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND — printed on the sheet that governs this room — includes 'SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY'. A555 kn3 reads 'IN BATHROOM LOCATIONS ONLY, LIGHT SWITCH EQUIPPED WITH NIGHTLIGHT', which only makes sense if switches exist outside the bath. The 'Entry / closet / general room lighting fixture(s)' line tells the walker to 'confirm each switches' but gives him no device line, no count, no height and no place to record what he found. This is the single most-touched device in the room.
defects.correction: Add: category Electrical, mark '—', label 'Entry / room lighting switch(es) — count and location not stated', qty 1 (placeholder, not a count), where 'Entry leg at the guestroom door and wherever else A555 view 04.1 dimensions a switch symbol', reliability FLAGGED, origin sheets-only, src 'E400 (switching: entry, bath); A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND "SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY"; A555 kn3 (bathroom-only qualifier); E101 spec #18 vs E101 symbol legend'. Note must carry the open height (E101 spec #18 = +54" AFF vs E101 symbol legend = 48" AFF) and state the count is unstated — the symbol is a graphic on A555 view 04.1, pull it off the PDF before the walk. verifyAtPunch: 'Operate every switch and record what each one controls; count them; measure to the top of each and write the number down.'
defects.citation: E400.md:27 ('switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)'); A550.md:230 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND; A550.md:124 kn3; E101.md:70 spec #18 and :77 symbol legend

defects.line: MISSING — no line for the dishwasher switch under the sink
defects.problem: E101 General Note 4 reads, verbatim, 'Dishwasher switches in cabinet under sink.' That is a punch-visible, operable device — the walker opens the cabinet door and flips it. A555 tags 902 DISHWASHER on the working wall and A550 kn10 ('DEDICATED CIRCUIT FOR DISHWASHER') is in A555's placed list for views 04/04.1, so the appliance and its circuit are both established for this room type. The list drops the dishwasher circuit as rough-in (correct) but never emits the switch at the visible end of it. It also interlocks with the unresolved SK-3/SK-4 kitchenette-sink line: if there is no sink there is no under-sink cabinet, so what the walker finds here is evidence on that open question.
defects.correction: Add: category Electrical, mark '—', label 'Dishwasher switch, in the cabinet under the sink', qty 1, where 'Kitchenette / working wall, inside the base cabinet under the sink', reliability MEDIUM, origin sheets-only, src 'E101 General Note 4; A555 kn10 (views 04/04.1); A555 tag 902 DISHWASHER'. Note: 'E101 GN4 verbatim: "Dishwasher switches in cabinet under sink." The location rides on the SK-3/SK-4 question — P401/P402 restrict the kitchenette sink to "the suite/extended units" and name no unit plan, so if there is no sink in this room there is no under-sink cabinet either. Record present or absent; that observation feeds the same open RFI.' verifyAtPunch: 'Open the base cabinet under the sink — switch present, flip it, dishwasher runs and stops.'
defects.citation: E101.md:74 General Note 4; A550.md:131 kn10; A555.md:114 (kn10 in the placed list for views 04/04.1); A555.md:70 (902 dishwasher tag)

defects.line: Electrical — 'Bathroom light switch with integrated LED night light, top of switch 48" MAX AFF' (reliability HIGH)
defects.problem: Two separate over-resolutions on one HIGH line. (1) A530 keyed note 24 reads verbatim 'LED NIGHT LIGHT INTEGRATED WITH EITHER LIGHT SWITCH OR OUTLET' — the sheet gives an option and the line adopts one side silently. E400 Keyed Note 1 and A555 kn3 say switch; A530 kn24 (placed on view 03, the door/shower wall of the very bathroom that governs this room) says either. The verify step 'Switch off — night-light LED must glow' will write up a compliant outlet-integrated night light as a deficiency. (2) The note asserts the 48" MAX 'is the one height the drawings state as a hard MAX rather than a target ... it is enforceable today, unlike the receptacle and thermostat heights.' E101 specification #18 states 'Switches at +54" AFF', and E101's own symbol legend shows the single-pole switch at 48" AFF — E101.md flags this in terms ('spec vs legend conflict on switch height ... Default to +54" per spec unless an RFI says otherwise'). A switch set at 54" satisfies E101 #18 and violates A555 kn3's MAX. That is two sheets disagreeing, and the list records one.
defects.correction: Downgrade to MEDIUM. Label: 'Bathroom light switch — LED night light integrated with EITHER the switch or the outlet (A530 kn24)'. Note must add: 'TWO READINGS ON THE DEVICE: A530 kn24 verbatim "LED NIGHT LIGHT INTEGRATED WITH EITHER LIGHT SWITCH OR OUTLET" — E400 KN1 and A555 kn3 both say switch, A530 kn24 permits the outlet. Record which one carries the LED; do NOT write up a switch without a night light until you have checked the GFCI outlet for one. TWO READINGS ON THE HEIGHT: 48" MAX to top of switch (A555 kn3, G402 GN1 context) vs +54" AFF (E101 spec #18, with E101's own symbol legend printing 48" — the set contradicts itself on its own rules sheet). Measure and record; this is C-03 territory, not an enforceable call.' verifyAtPunch: 'With the room dark, confirm a night-light LED glows and record whether it is in the switch or the outlet; measure to the top of the switch and write the number down.'
defects.citation: A530.md:168 keyed note 24 (and :43, kn24 placed on view 03); E400.md:47 Keyed Note 1; A550.md:124 kn3; E101.md:70 spec #18, :77 symbol legend, :87 and :94 (the flagged conflict)

defects.line: Reconciler self-report, 'other' — 'The 15"-48" guest-control band and the 30"x48" clear floor area are NOT enforceable here' (applied throughout the list, and load-bearing on the thermostat line)
defects.problem: This is a resolution, not a reading, and the sheets contradict it. A530's GENERAL NOTES - GUESTROOMS note F — printed identically on all five bath sheets including the one that governs room 101's bathroom — reads verbatim 'ALL CONTROLS FOR USE BY GUESTS MUST BE MOUNTED @ B/T 15" A.F.F. & 48" A.F.F. & PROVIDE A 30"X48" CLEAR FLOOR AREA IN COMPLIANCE W/ ACCESSIBLE STANDARDS.' It carries NO accessible-room qualifier — and the contrast is deliberate, because the very next two notes do: note G opens 'IN ACCESSIBLE ROOMS AT LEAST ONE OUTLET & DATA CONNECTION...' and note H opens 'OBJECTS MOUNTED W/IN THE CIRCULATION PATH IN ACCESSIBLE ROOMS...'. G402 note 11 is likewise unqualified ('ALL CONTROLS FOR USE BY GUESTS, MUST BE MOUNTED BETWEEN 15" AFF AND 48" AFF'), and coordination_issues C-03's own table logs G402 note 11 against the element 'ALL CONTROLS FOR USE BY GUESTS' with no accessible scoping. This matters concretely: it is the only thing letting M401 KN4's 54" non-accessible thermostat stand un-contradicted in this room, and the thermostat line never cites note F at all.
defects.correction: Strike the blanket exclusion. Replace with: 'A530 GENERAL NOTE F is UNQUALIFIED and applies on its face to this room — notes G and H are expressly scoped to accessible rooms, F is not. Carried as a fourth source on every guest-control height.' Add A530 GN F and G402 note 11 to the src on the thermostat, convenience-receptacle, data, TV and telephone lines, and restate the thermostat conflict as FOUR values, matching C-03: 48" (A555 KN24, M101 GN29, G402 note 11, G400) · 54" non-accessible (M401 KN4) · 60" (E101 symbol legend) · ≤46" over an obstruction deeper than 10" (G402 note 11). Keep the do-not-write-up instruction.
defects.citation: A530.md:183-185 general notes F, G, H (identical on A531, A532, A532.1, A533); G402.md:175 note 11 and :162 schedule note 4; coordination_issues.md:75-79 C-03 table

defects.line: Fire Protection — 'Addressable photoelectric smoke detector — Silent Knight SKPHOTOW in a System Sensor B200S-LF-WH ... COUNT IS SOLID' (reliability HIGH)
defects.problem: The reliability is one grade above what the source supports for THIS room type. packages/fire-appliance.md's own per-type table rates the row 'QQ Connecting · QQ Extended · QQ Wide · QQ Wide Connecting · QQ Acc. · King Studio Connecting · King Studio Acc.' at MEDIUM and states in terms that it was '**not** read off FA-2/FA-3 for these types' — it rests on E501–E504 + E400 + the 121-schedule arithmetic. The line instead cites 'FA-2/FA-3 verified on 303/305/307/311' — none of which is a QQ Wide Connecting — and declares 'COUNT IS SOLID ... floor 1 is a flat 1 per key with no exceptions.' This is the same extraction gap the list flagged loudly for sprinklers on this exact room, un-flagged one line down. The 121/121 arithmetic does reconcile (115 keys + 6 second detectors in the 6 one-bedroom units, and A100's matrix confirms 3 King One Bdr + 2 ACC HA + 1 ACC HA CD = 6), so the count is well-argued — but well-argued arithmetic is MEDIUM, not HIGH.
defects.correction: Downgrade to MEDIUM. Amend the note: 'COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT READ FOR THIS ROOM TYPE. FA-1's 121/121 reconciles exactly to 115 keys + the 6 second detectors in the 6 one-bedroom suites, and A100's matrix puts no one-bedroom on floor 1 — so 1 per key is sound arithmetic. But packages/fire-appliance.md rates QQ Wide Connecting MEDIUM and states the row was NOT read off FA-2/FA-3 for this type; the 303/305/307/311 verifications are other room types. SETTLES IT: read the FA-2 first-floor region for 101 — the same document-reading task that closes the sprinkler row.' Everything else on the line (the LF sounder base as the audible appliance, the 75 dBA vs 15-over-ambient conflict, the two addresses, the red FA plates per E500 note 10) is correct and should stay.
defects.citation: packages/fire-appliance.md:278 and :468; FA-1 schedule row (S)SB 121/121 at fire-appliance.md:164; A100.md GUESTROOM MATRIX (King One Bdr 3 + King One Bdr ACC HA 2 + King One Bdr ACC HA CD 1 = 6)

defects.line: Fire Protection — 'Viking sprinkler heads on drop, K=4.3 ... mark ◉ VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD (ASSUMED)', src 'FP-1 head schedule (62 heads 1st floor / 437 all floors)'
defects.problem: FP-1's head schedule has TWO rows and the line cites one. The second is ⊗ — 73 heads first floor / 101 all floors — model 'VK462 1/2 QR 155 B CC', K=5.6, ON DROP. On floor 1 the VK462 outnumbers the VK430, 73 to 62. The line imports the package's '~90% ASSUMPTION' without noting that the 90% is a BUILDING-WIDE figure (437 of 547); on floor 1 specifically the VK430 share is 62 of 135, about 46%. The '(ASSUMED — not read for this room)' flag is therefore materially weaker than the note lets on, and a reader is told the wrong odds on the one floor he is walking tomorrow.
defects.correction: Amend the note: 'FP-1 SCHEDULES TWO HEAD TYPES AND FLOOR 1 IS MOSTLY THE OTHER ONE. Row ◉ = 62 first floor / 437 all floors, VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD, K=4.3, 1/2" thread, ON DROP. Row ⊗ = 73 first floor / 101 all floors, VK462 1/2 QR 155 B CC, K=5.6, ON DROP. The package's ~90%-VK430 assumption is building-wide; on FLOOR 1 the VK430 is 62 of 135 heads, roughly 46%. Do not treat VK430 as the likely model in this room — READ THE MODEL OFF THE INSTALLED HEAD or the FP-1 region, and record it.' Add the VK462 model string to the verify step.
defects.citation: packages/fire-appliance.md:39-40, FP-1 head schedule rows ◉ and ⊗

defects.line: Fire Protection — sprinkler line 'where': 'Guest-room ceilings — expect bed/window area, living/sofa area, and entry/kitchenette leg'
defects.problem: The A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND — the legend printed on the architectural sheet that governs this room — carries THREE distinct sprinkler symbols: 'SIDE WALL SPRINKLER HEAD', 'SPRINKLER HEAD' and 'SIDE WALL SPRINKLER HEAD (D)'. The line's where is ceilings only and its verify ('COUNT the heads in the room ... record flush cover plate or escutcheon-with-deflector; confirm NONE in the bath') sends the walker looking up. A side-wall head is a wall device with a different trim and a different look; a count taken from the ceiling alone is wrong, and this is the one line whose entire purpose is to produce a defensible count.
defects.correction: Change where to: 'Guest-room ceilings AND walls — the A550/A555 power & signal legend prints pendent, side-wall and side-wall (D) sprinkler symbols, so heads may be wall-mounted. NOT in the bathroom (no head is drawn in either verified room's bath).' verifyAtPunch: 'COUNT every head in the room — ceiling AND wall — and write the number and type of each down; record flush cover plate or escutcheon-with-deflector; confirm NONE in the bath.'
defects.citation: A550.md:230 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND (identical on A555 per A555.md:129); packages/fire-appliance.md:87

defects.line: Electrical — 'Convenience duplex receptacles, tamper-resistant, 20 A, Hubbell or approved equal'
defects.problem: The label and the whole line assume duplex. The A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND prints 'OUTLET - DUPLEX', 'OUTLET - DUPLEX - GFI', 'OUTLET - QUAD' and 'OUTLET - QUAD - GFI' as four separate guestroom symbols, and E101's symbol legend independently carries 'quad/quad-duplex receptacle'. On a line that already concedes 'QTY IS NOT STATED ON ANY SHEET', normalising four device types down to one is the same class of error as tidying a mark. A walker told to count 'convenience duplex receptacles' has no instruction for a quad and will either miscount it as one duplex or as two.
defects.correction: Relabel: 'Convenience receptacles — DUPLEX and QUAD, tamper-resistant, 20 A, Hubbell or approved equal'. Add to the note: 'DEVICE TYPE IS ALSO UNSTATED. A555 prints four receptacle symbols in its power & signal legend — duplex, duplex-GFI, quad and quad-GFI — and which symbol lands at each dimensioned point on view 04.1 is readable only off the PDF. Count and record duplex and quad SEPARATELY.' Add 'A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND' to the src.
defects.citation: A550.md:230 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND; E101.md:77 symbol legend

defects.line: Electrical — 'Surface-mount ceiling downlight, guest bathroom — Cooper Halo SMD6R69SWH' (src '...E400; E201') and 'Entry / closet / general room lighting fixture(s)' (src 'E400 ...; E201 ("entry/closet lights")')
defects.problem: E201 is the LIGHTING AND POWER SECOND FLOOR PLAN. Room 101 is on the first floor. The 'entry/closet lights' phrase does appear on E201, but as a description of second-floor guestrooms. The first-floor sheet is E200, and E200 states in terms that guestroom lighting is not drawn on it: 'West ~half — GUESTROOM wing: shaded; lighting not shown here — two callouts "Refer to Enlarged Guestroom Plan (E-400)."' Citing a second-floor plan as a source on a first-floor room sheet is the kind of thing that gets a punch list dismissed in a meeting.
defects.correction: Drop E201 from both src strings. For the entry/closet line the honest src is 'E400 (fixtures present, untyped); A555 view 04 printed note "CENTER OVER CLOSET"' with a note that E200 explicitly defers first-floor guestroom lighting to E400 — which strengthens rather than weakens the point that no type is named anywhere. For the S21 line: 'E101 Lighting Fixture Schedule row S21; E400'.

defects.line: Mechanical — 'Ceiling fire / radiation damper ... Ruskin CFD4' and 'Access panel in the bath ceiling ... with permanent damper label' (both cite M501 for the label requirement)
defects.problem: Both lines attribute the labelling requirement to M501 — 'M501 requires approved access with a permanent label reading FIRE DAMPER in letters min 1/2" high'. M501 detail 2 (Ceiling/Radiation Fire Damper, Ruskin CFD4, UL 555C, ceramic-fibre shroud, 3"x3" galvanised angle, sheet-metal duct throughout) contains no label requirement. The requirement is M101 General Notes 31–32: fire/smoke dampers 'provide approved access w/ permanent exterior label (≥0.5" letters) reading FIRE/SMOKE DAMPER, SMOKE DAMPER, or FIRE DAMPER.' The access-panel line is described as 'the single most transferable finding on the walk' — it needs the right sheet on it.
defects.correction: Move the label citation to M101 GN31/GN32 on both lines (both already list M101 GN31/GN32 in src, so it is only the note prose that is wrong). Keep M501 det.2 cited for the CFD4 model, the UL 555C listing, the fusible link and the sheet-metal-not-flex requirement, which is what M501 actually carries.
defects.citation: M501.md detail 2; M101.md:50 N31-N32

defects.line: Electrical — 'Garbage-disposal switch ganged with a duplex receptacle' (note: "kn14 verbatim: 'SWITCH CONTROLLING GARBAGE DISPOSAL GANGED WITH DUPLEX'"), and Low Voltage — WAP line (note: 'kn44 verbatim: ...')
defects.problem: Both quotes are labelled 'verbatim' and both are truncated. A550 kn14 in full: 'SWITCH CONTROLLING GARBAGE DISPOSAL GANGED WITH DUPLEX - REFER TO HADG FOR ACCESSIBLE ROOM REQUIREMENTS'. A550 kn44 in full ends: '...COORDINATE WAP LOCATION WITH CASEGOODS TO AVOID CONFLICTS. VISIT CONNECTEDROOM.HILTON.COM FOR CURRENT WIRELESS INTERNET REQ'S AND LIST OF APPROVED INTEGRATORS' — the clause the WAP note then relies on for the integrator requirement is inside the keynote it just truncated. On a list whose credibility rests on quoting the sheet, 'verbatim' has to mean verbatim.
defects.correction: Restore both full strings, or mark the truncation with an ellipsis and drop the word 'verbatim'.

defects.line: Plumbing — 'Lavatory bowl, undermount rectangular — Decolav Callensia 1402-CWH', mark 'L-2 / L-3 / L-4'
defects.problem: Two things. (1) The note says 'P401/P402 print L-2 on the unit plans'. They do not — both sheets print the guestroom lavatory as 'L-2 / L-3'. P401: 'lavatory (L-2 / L-3)'. P402: 'L-2 / L-3 (lavatory)'. (2) The three-way composite 'L-2 / L-3 / L-4' is not printed on any sheet — it is the DB's carry-both convention, exactly as 'PTAC-2 / PTAC-1' is. The list flags the PTAC composite explicitly ('no sheet prints the composite string') and does not flag this one, or the equivalent 'SH-1 / SH-4'. Inconsistent treatment of the same defect class.
defects.correction: Fix the note to 'P401/P402 print L-2 / L-3 on the unit plans; P104 schedules the guestroom lav as L-3 / L-4.' Add to both this line and the shower line: 'The composite mark as printed here is the DB's carry-both convention. No sheet prints it. Do not put it on a purchase document.' — the same sentence already carried on the PTAC row.

defects.line: Mechanical — 'Energy-management wall controller with occupancy sensor', where: 'Wall in the bedroom near the PTAC / window wall'
defects.problem: The line cites A555 KN24 as a source and then places the device on the window wall. KN24 is placed on A555 view 07 — 'ELEVATION (bed wall + sofa wall)'. A555 view 08, the window wall, carries keynotes 1 and 4 only. No sheet places any control device on the window wall. The thermostat line one row down gets this right ('Bed wall / sofa wall — A555 view 07 carries KN24'), so the list contradicts itself on the location of what may be the same physical device — which is precisely the open question the line exists to record.
defects.correction: Change where to: 'Bed wall / sofa wall — the only control device A555 places is KN24 on view 07. No sheet places a second control device anywhere, and none is placed on the window wall (view 08 carries keynotes 1 and 4 only).' That sharpens rather than weakens the one-device-or-two flag.
defects.citation: A555.md:122 (view 07 keynotes) and :123 (view 08 keynotes 1, 4)

defects.line: Plumbing — 'Floor drain, guestroom bathroom' (reliability FLAGGED, 'the quantity may be 1 or ZERO')
defects.problem: A third in-set source pointing at a drain in a STANDARD guest bath is not on the row. E400's guestroom General Note 4 reads 'Slope floors to drain; slope ≤ 1:48 any direction' — printed on the typical-guestroom sheet, governing all six enlarged plans including 'QQ Studio (Detail 05) — Panel A', the standard non-accessible plan. A note that requires the floor to be sloped to a drain presupposes a drain. That does not close the P402-vs-A530 conflict, but it does mean the FOR side has two sources, not one, and the line as written gives the walker the impression it is 50/50.
defects.correction: Add E400 GN4 to the src and to the note: 'A THIRD SOURCE ON THE FOR SIDE: E400 general note 4 (typical guestroom, all six enlarged plans including the standard QQ Studio / Panel A) requires "slope floors to drain, slope ≤ 1:48 any direction" — a slope-to-drain requirement on the standard plan implies a drain on the standard plan. Still not resolved against P402's accessible-units-only placement; both readings carried.' Everything else on the line — no mark, no scheduled product, FD-1/FD-2/FD-3 all being other spaces — checks out exactly against P104.
defects.citation: E400.md:52 General Note 4; A530.md:164 keyed note 20; P402.md:22; P104.md Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule

defects.line: Plumbing — 'Water closet, floor outlet, tank type, 1.28 GPF ...' note: 'A530 kn21 (lever opposite the inside corner) is an ACCESSIBLE-room note and does NOT apply here'
defects.problem: Right conclusion, invented reason. No sheet says kn21 is an accessible-room note. The BATHROOM KEYED NOTES legend is printed identically on A530, A531, A532, A532.1 and A533, so legend membership says nothing about which sheet places a note. The actual reason kn21 does not apply is simpler and checkable: A530 does not PLACE keyed note 21 on any view. A530's placed keynotes are 12, 22, 30, 19, 9, 20, 23, 27 (plan 01) · 23, 16, 13, 24 (view 03) · 28, 23, 16, 14 (view 04) · 9, 14, 23, 30 (view 05). Stating a scope rule the sheet does not state is the exact defect class this list polices everywhere else.
defects.correction: Replace with: 'A530 does not PLACE keyed note 21 (tank lever opposite the inside corner) on any view — its placed keynotes are 12, 22, 30, 19, 9, 20, 23, 27 on plan 01 and 13/14/16/23/24/28/30 on the elevations. The note sits in the shared legend printed on all five bath sheets, so legend membership proves nothing. Nothing requires a lever orientation in this room.'
defects.citation: A530.md:36, :43, :46, :48 (placed keynotes by view); A530.md:3 and :165 (shared legend, kn21)

defects.line: Plumbing — 'Trap guard / trap primer at the bathroom floor drain'
defects.problem: The line names two trap-PRIMER products and misses the one trap-GUARD product the set actually schedules. P104's Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule attaches 'w/ trap guard TG-1' to FD-1, FD-2 and FS — TG-1 is the only trap-guard mark anywhere in the set, and like the two primers it is scoped to drains that are not the guestroom drain. The verify step says 'Lift the strainer — trap guard fitted' and gives the walker nothing to check it against, when the sheet does at least name a mark.
defects.correction: Add to the note: 'THE ONLY TRAP GUARD SCHEDULED IN THE SET IS TG-1, and P104 attaches it to FD-1 (Mech/Laundry), FD-2 (Unfinished) and FS (Floor Sink) — not to any guestroom drain. So all three devices in play here (Sioux Chief 695, TP-1 PPP SMP-500-115V, TG-1) are scheduled to somewhere other than a guest bath, while P301 note 6 and P501 det.12 require one at every floor drain. Record what is fitted and its make.'
defects.citation: P104.md:72-75 (TG-1 on FD-1, FD-2, FS); P301.md:52 note 6; P501.md detail 12; P102.md:39 (Sioux Chief 695)

defects.line: Mechanical — 'Volume damper at the toilet exhaust, with locking quadrant', src 'M401 ...; M101 legend + GN25/GN26; M301 GN11; M101 GN7'
defects.problem: M101 N25 reads 'Each SUPPLY outlet gets its own balancing device.' The EAG-50 is an exhaust grille, not a supply outlet, so N25 does not reach it. The citation that does is M301 General Note 11 ('balancing damper each branch/runout') and M101 N26 (manual balancing dampers have locking quadrant) — both already on the row. The stray N25 makes the line look better-sourced than it is, on a line that is already an admitted arguable scope call.
defects.correction: Drop GN25 from the src; keep M101 GN26 (locking quadrant), M301 GN11 (balancing damper each branch/runout), M401 (EAG-50 with VD and FD) and M101 GN7 (min 12"x12" access to dampers). The argument for keeping the line IN is unaffected.
defects.citation: M101.md:47 N25-N26; M301.md General Note 11

defects.line: Mechanical — 'PTAC condensate drain — 1" VISIBLE drain with 1" air-gap fitting, run down the wall' (label)
defects.problem: The label lists the drain and the air-gap fitting and omits the trap, which is the part that actually fails and the part a walker can see. P501 detail 13 (Condensate Drain Detail) shows air gap, 1" P-TRAP, 1" VENT, 1" condensate riser to the 4" main. P301 and P302 both add '1" condensate line with 1-1/2" vent up (typ.)'. A P-trap on a condensate line either exists or it does not, and it is on the visible run the line is already sending the walker to trace. Separately, the sheet-typo catch is correct and worth keeping — P301 does send you to P502 for the condensate detail and P502 has no such detail; it is P501 det.13.
defects.correction: Label: 'PTAC condensate drain — 1" VISIBLE drain with 1" air-gap fitting and 1" P-trap, run down the wall'. verifyAtPunch: 'Run the PTAC in cooling — trace the visible drain down the wall, confirm the air-gap fitting is present and not taped over, confirm a trap is formed and holding, no stain.'
defects.citation: P501.md detail 13; P301.md:30; P302.md:25
